headline: A tiny parasite makes over 1,000 people sick

sources.title: STAT: Outbreak of diarrhea-causing parasite grows to more than 1,000 cases
CNN: An outbreak of diarrhea caused by a parasite has hit thousands of people
Cyclospora outbreak spreads to 47 US States | DW News (video, DW News)

chunks.text: Health officials say a tiny [[parasite]] called cyclospora has {{broken out}} across the United States. The CDC reported that this [[outbreak]] has made more than 1,000 people sick [[so far this year]]. The parasite is [[microscopic]], so people cannot see it on their food. Health officials are working to {{find out}} where the [[contaminated]] food comes from.

verbs.wrong: To move from animals to people
To test food in a laboratory
verbs.correct: To discover a fact after searching

chunks.text: Cyclospora usually [[spreads]] through contaminated fresh [[produce]], [[such as]] fruits and vegetables. When people {{come down with}} the [[illness]], they often have [[long-lasting]] [[diarrhea]] and stomach pain. The [[infection]], which doctors call cyclosporiasis, is not usually dangerous. Still, some patients {{end up}} needing [[medical care]] to {{deal with}} their [[symptoms]].

chunks.text: Health officials say the [[germs]] can get onto fresh food when [[irrigation]] water on farms is dirty. The CDC is {{looking into}} the outbreak, and its scientists are {{carrying out}} tests to learn more about it. Officials also [[warn of]] [[the danger of]] eating unwashed produce. They want people to be careful at home.

verbs.wrong: To count the number of sick people
To share results with the public
verbs.correct: To do or complete a task

chunks.text: [[To stay safe]], health officials tell people to {{wash off}} fresh fruits and vegetables under [[running water]]. Washing can help {{get rid of}} many germs, but it may not [[remove]] every one. Experts also suggest buying whole [[heads of lettuce]] and removing the outer leaves. Cooking vegetables can {{cut down on}} the [[risk]] of getting sick too.

mainIdea.s: A parasite called cyclospora has broken out across the United States and made more than 1,000 people sick this year. Officials are trying to find its source.
mainIdea.why: The article says cyclospora has sickened more than 1,000 people this year, and officials are looking into the source.

mainIdea.s: A new illness is spreading from person to person across the country, sickening more than a thousand people. Doctors say most patients need hospital care.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the illness does not spread from person to person. The article says cyclospora spreads through contaminated produce.

mainIdea.s: Last year, an outbreak linked to bagged salad sickened dozens of people in several states. Stores pulled the packages, and officials traced it to one farm.
mainIdea.why: This describes a separate outbreak linked to bagged salad. The article is about a cyclospora outbreak this year.

tf.s: The CDC is washing off the outbreak to learn more about it.
tf.why: The CDC is looking into the outbreak. Wash off means to clean something with water, so it does not describe studying the outbreak.

tf.s: Health officials are carrying out tests to study the outbreak.
tf.why: The scientists really are doing tests. Carry out means to do or complete a task, so this is correct.

tf.s: Some sick people end up needing medical care.
tf.why: A few patients do reach that final situation. End up means to reach a final result, so this is correct.

tf.s: To stay safe, doctors tell people to cut down on fresh fruit and vegetables.
tf.why: Doctors want people to wash off (clean) fresh fruit and vegetables before eating. Cut down on means to reduce something, which is not the advice.

tf.s: Cyclospora usually spreads through fruits and vegetables watered with clean, safe irrigation water
tf.why: The article says the parasite gets onto produce specifically when farm irrigation water is dirty, not clean, so this version is unambiguously false.

tf.s: The CDC is looking into the cause of the outbreak.
tf.why: Correct. The CDC is looking into (investigating) the outbreak. Look into means to try to find out about something.
